newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS- Straddles traded in BP, Shell.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- Straddles traded in BP, Shell.

text.p: Long-dated volatility trades in oil stocks were amongst the larger deals struck in the London equities options market on Friday, dealers said.
The main deals were a long straddle in Shell Transport & Trading and short straddle in British Petroleum. Both deals were done by one broker.
The deal in Shell concerned 1,000 January 1050 calls and puts bought at 75p and 62p each which if held to expiry will make a profit if the shares either go below 913p or above 1187p.
The deal in BP involved selling 1,500 January 700 calls and puts at 41p and 55p each.
For the short straddle to make the maximum profit of 96p, BP shares need to be 700p at expiry.
By 1430 GMT, BP shares had slipped a penny to 682p while those of Shell were up 8p to 1046-1/2p.

Similarly, over in hotels and leisure company Ladbroke Group there was a buyer of 1,000 August 240 calls and puts -- at 13-1/2p each -- in a long straddle strategy and half of these were subsequently sold to another trader at the same prices. Ladbroke shares slipped 1/2p to 235p.
Elsewhere, a bullish deal was struck in National Power by selling out-of-the-money puts.

The deal was the sale of 1,250 June 460 puts at 8p and this will be the maximum profit if the shares stay above 460p by June expiry. And in building materials group Tarmac there was a seller of 1,000 June 110 calls at 10p.
National Power fell 9-1/2p to 5190-1/2p and Tarmac was unchanged at 116p.
Tobacco-to-insurance group B.A.T Indusries also attracted attention, mainly from buyers of call options and a couple of traders bought 250 July 550 calls at 28p. The shares were down 9p to 530p.
